The measured football evidence leans toward Oklahoma, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Oklahoma has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Oklahoma’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.6% of its dropbacks, and South Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Oklahoma has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Oklahoma’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 17.0% of its runs, and South Carolina’s defense stops 21.4% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When South Carolina has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): South Carolina’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.6% of its runs, and Oklahoma’s defense stops 16.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put South Carolina’s offensive line No. 26 nationally and Oklahoma’s No. 99.
contradicting: When South Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): South Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.0% of its dropbacks, and Oklahoma’s defense sacks the quarterback on 10.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Oklahoma has the ball (big plays through the air): Oklahoma’s offense turns 12.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and South Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 12.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Oklahoma’s secondary No. 7 nationally and South Carolina’s No. 80.
quarterbacks: John Mateer has completed 136 of 205 passes (66.3%) for 1,611 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in seven games for Oklahoma, and has been sacked on 16 of 221 dropbacks.

LaNorris Sellers has completed 133 of 220 passes (60.5%) for 1,548 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for South Carolina, and has been sacked on 15 of 235 dropbacks.
